title: Empirical Analysis of Cybersecurity Trust Deficits in QR-Based Mobile Payment Adoption Among Semi-Rural Malaysian Micro-Enterprises

objectives.text: To identify and evaluate the specific cybersecurity trust barriers and fraud vulnerabilities impacting semi-rural micro-merchants in Johor.
To develop and empirically test an extended UTAUT2 structural model incorporating perceived transaction risk and merchant discount rate frictions.
To formulate actionable policy and technical recommendations for Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and fintech payment operators.

key_milestones.title: Proposal Defense & Theoretical Framework Approval
key_milestones.description: Synthesize literature review, finalize survey instrument, and present to faculty defense committee.

key_milestones.title: Pilot Study & Instrument Validation
key_milestones.description: Administer pilot questionnaire to 30 micro-retailers in Iskandar Malaysia; test Cronbach's alpha and composite reliability.

key_milestones.title: Field Data Collection & SEM Modeling
key_milestones.description: Collect complete cross-sectional data from 250 SME merchants across Johor commercial corridors; conduct PLS-SEM analysis in SmartPLS.

key_milestones.title: Thesis Submission & Viva Voce
key_milestones.description: Finalize thesis chapters, submit dissertation draft for examiner review, and defend in oral examination.

necessary_resources.justification: Mandatory prior to field survey distribution involving small business proprietors.

tasks: Synthesize OpenAlex and UTM literature base
Formulate conceptual framework based on UTAUT2
Administer survey to 250 micro-retailers across Johor
Perform data screening, normality, and multi-collinearity checks
Interpret hypothesis testing results and discuss theoretical implications
Draft recommendations for BNM digital blueprint
Complete thesis revision and viva voce defense

methodology_summary: Cross-sectional quantitative survey design. Target sample of 250 semi-rural micro-merchants in Johor analyzed via PLS-SEM to evaluate cybersecurity risk moderations on continuous e-wallet persistence.
